items.stem: The natural rate of unemployment is
options: the rate of unemployment in a recession
the rate of unemployment when the labour market is in equilibrium, consisting of frictional and structural unemployment
items.answer: the rate of unemployment when the labour market is in equilibrium, consisting of frictional and structural unemployment

items.stem: Explain why the natural rate of unemployment is not zero.
items.answer: Workers take time to search between jobs (frictional) and skills or locations may not match vacancies (structural); these exist even when the labour market clears.

items.stem: Explain two factors that may raise the natural rate of unemployment.
items.answer: Generous benefits reducing search intensity; occupational and geographical immobility; minimum wages above equilibrium; trade union power; technological change; poor information.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each identified, 1 mark each explained [4]

items.stem: In Loristan, 42.6 million people are employed and 1.5 million are unemployed. Calculate the unemployment rate.

In Westaria, 24 million people are employed and 0.6 million unemployed. Of the unemployed, 0.18 million are frictionally unemployed, 0.24 million structurally unemployed and the rest are cyclically unemployed. Calculate the unemployment rate and the natural rate of unemployment, and explain which type of unemployment demand-side policy could reduce.
items.answer: Unemployment rate = 2.4%; natural rate = (0.18 + 0.24)/24.6 × 100 = 1.7%. Demand-side policy can reduce the cyclical (0.18 million) unemployment.
items.markingKey: LF = 24.6 [1]; rate [1]; natural rate = frictional + structural [1]; cyclical is demand-deficient, so addressed by demand-side policy [1].

items.stem: In Valdoria, 9.4 million people are employed and 1.2 million unemployed. Of the unemployed, 0.3 million are frictionally unemployed, 0.36 million structurally unemployed and the rest are cyclically unemployed. Calculate the unemployment rate and the natural rate of unemployment, and explain which type of unemployment demand-side policy could reduce.
items.answer: Unemployment rate = 11.3%; natural rate = (0.3 + 0.36)/10.6 × 100 = 6.2%. Demand-side policy can reduce the cyclical (0.54 million) unemployment.
items.markingKey: LF = 10.6 [1]; rate [1]; natural rate = frictional + structural [1]; cyclical is demand-deficient, so addressed by demand-side policy [1].

items.answer: (a) 3.3 percentage points; 73.3% (b) Occupational and geographical immobility; skills mismatch; information gaps.

items.stem: Unemployment in Dravonia is 4%, close to its estimated natural rate. Explain why a large increase in government spending might raise inflation rather than employment.
items.answer: At the natural rate there is no demand-deficient unemployment; extra AD pushes unemployment below the NAIRU only temporarily, creating excess demand for labour and accelerating inflation.

items.stem: Voluntary unemployment occurs when
options: workers choose not to accept jobs at the current wage rate
workers are willing to work at the current wage but cannot find jobs
items.answer: workers choose not to accept jobs at the current wage rate
items.markingKey: Natural unemployment: gap between labour force (LF) and those willing to accept jobs (AJ) at the equilibrium wage.

items.stem: With the aid of a diagram, explain the natural rate of unemployment using the AJ and LF curves.
items.answer: Diagram: real wage on vertical axis, labour on horizontal; ADL (demand) downward; AJ curve (those willing to accept jobs) upward; LF curve to the right of AJ. Equilibrium where ADL = AJ gives employment Le at real wage We; the horizontal gap between AJ and LF at We is the natural rate (voluntary) unemployment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: curves; 1 mark: equilibrium; 1 mark: gap AJ–LF [3]

items.stem: Explain how greater labour market flexibility can reduce unemployment and one disadvantage of it.
items.answer: Flexible wages and hours allow the labour market to clear quickly, firms hire more readily if they can adjust staff, and workers move between jobs; disadvantage: job insecurity, low pay and zero-hours contracts may reduce worker welfare and training.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: mechanism; 1 mark: reduced unemployment; 1 mark: disadvantage [3]

items.stem: In Dravonia, at the equilibrium real wage of $15 an hour, 37.5 million people are willing to accept jobs (AJ) and the labour force (LF) is 40 million. Calculate the natural (voluntary) unemployment.
items.answer: 2.5 million

items.stem: In Korvia, at the equilibrium real wage of $12 an hour, 28.5 million people are willing to accept jobs (AJ) and the labour force (LF) is 30 million. A minimum wage of $14 is introduced; at this wage firms demand 27 million workers, AJ = 29 million and LF = 30.2 million. Calculate the natural unemployment before the change, and the voluntary and involuntary unemployment after it.
items.answer: Before: natural unemployment 1.5 million. After: involuntary (real-wage) unemployment = AJ − Ld = 2 million; voluntary = LF − AJ = 1.2 million; total 3.2 million.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: LF − AJ before; 1 mark: involuntary = AJ − Ld at Wmin; 1 mark: voluntary = LF − AJ; 1 mark: total [4]

items.stem: The labour force participation rate is

employment as a percentage of the total population

items.stem: Explain two policies to reduce frictional unemployment.
items.answer: Better information on vacancies (job centres, online matching); lower benefit replacement rates or conditional benefits to raise search intensity; help with relocation costs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each identified, 1 mark each explained [4]

items.stem: Explain why a rise in labour productivity might lead to higher unemployment in the short run but lower unemployment in the long run.
items.answer: Short run: the same output needs fewer workers. Long run: lower unit costs make firms more competitive, raise real incomes and demand, and create new jobs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: short-run effect; 1 mark: long-run competitiveness/demand [2]
